Analysis by Richard Cowan

(MarijuanaNews note: Several of these stories occurred before I resumed updating

MarijuanaNews.com in August, but I have tried to find relevant items from the

archives.

There has been some progress toward freedom this year, but the prohibitionist

police state is on the counterattack. The commitment by the leading Democratic

Presidential candidates to “stop the raids” on California medical cannabis

dispensaries has spurred the narks to action to try to destroy the movement in

California before 2009.

On the other hand, their actions are further alienating the public. It is called

“blowback.” It remains to be seen what will happen to the energy unleashed by the

Ron Paul phenomenon if he does poorly in the initial primaries. If he does well, then

it will really scramble American politics. As I have said, the reason that I am

working with Steve Kubby is to see that the cannabis issues – and the drug war in

general – become a part of the public agenda.)

See

Why the Libertarian Party and Movement Are Especially Important to the

Marijuana Reform Movement This Y ear. Ron Paul and Beyond with Steve Kubby.

December 27, 2007 - Washington, DC, USA

#1 DEA Steps Up Attacks Against California Medi-Pot Patients, Dispensaries

Federal law enforcement officials took unprecedented steps in 2007 to quash California’s

medi-pot patient community. DEA officials raided a record number of dispensaries and

mailed hundreds of letters to California landlords threatening them with arrest and up to

20 years imprisonment, as well as the forfeiture of their building, if they rented to

medicinal cannabis clubs. Since DEA officials began mailing warning letters this summer,

numerous high profile clubs across the state have ceased operations. Read the full story at:

http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7452.

#2 DEA Administrative Law Judge Rules Against US Government's Monopoly On Pot

Production

DEA Administrative Law Judge Mary Ellen Bittner ruled in February that the private

production of cannabis for research purposes is “in the public interest.” She found that the

DEA had improperly rejected an application from the University of Massachusetts at

Amherst to manufacture cannabis for FDA-approved research. The agency has yet to

affirm or set aside the ruling. Read the full story at:

http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7176.

(MarijuanaNews note: Unfortunately, the DEA has a record of ignoring the rulings

of its own Administrative Law Judges.

In 1988, after two years of hearings, Francis L. Young, then chief DEA

Administrative Law Judge, concluded that the evidence "clearly shows that

marijuana has been accepted as capable of relieving the distress of great numbers of

very ill people, and doing so with safety under medical supervision. It would be

unreasonable, arbitrary, and capricious for DEA to continue to stand between those

sufferers and the benefits of this substance." He also said that marijuana is "one of

the safest therapeutically active substances known...."

Nonetheless, the DEA director at the time, John Lawn, simply rejected Young’s

findings. Lawn’s ruling was eventually upheld when NORML appealed the decision

to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia. The court simply said that

the DEA director had the power to overrule its ALJ. I expect the same outcome in

this case. They are not about to let real research be done with med cannabis any

more than they will allow farmers to grow hemp.)

#3 Pot Compounds Inhibit Spread Of Breast Cancer, Lung Cancer

Compounds in marijuana reduce the spread and size of various cancers, including lung

cancer and breast cancer, according to a pair of preclinical studies published in 2007. In

the first, investigators at Harvard University reported that THC reduced lung tumor

growth by as much as 50 percent compared to untreated controls. In the second trial,

researchers at California Pacific Medical Center Research Institute reported that CBD

significantly limits the activity of a gene linked to the spread of breast cancer. Read the full

story at: http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7433.

#4: Marijuana Arrests For Year 2005 Most Ever

Police arrested an estimated 829,625 persons for marijuana violations in 2006, the highest

annual total ever recorded in the United States, according to statistics compiled in

September by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. An American is now arrested for

violating marijuana laws every 38 seconds. Read the full story at:

http://norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7370.

See

More Arresting Developments. Record Marijuana Arrests Go Unreported. “No

Medicine Is Smoked” – So DEA Busts Edibles Maker.

#5 New Mexico Becomes Twelfth State To Authorize Medical Cannabis Use

New Mexico lawmakers approved legislation in April approving the use of medicinal

cannabis by authorized patients. New Mexico is the twelfth state since 1996 to enact

legislation protecting medical cannabis patients from arrest and state criminal prosecution,

though it is only the fourth to do so legislatively. Lawmakers in Rhode Island, Vermont,

and Washington amended their medical marijuana laws in 2007. Read the full story at:

http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7231.

(MarijuanaNews note: New Mexico Governor Bill Richardson’s bid for the

Democratic Presidential nomination is not going well, but the other candidates know

that he was not hurt by his support for medical marijuana.)

#6 Studies Find That Cannabis Has “Clear Medical Benefits” For HIV Patients

Inhaling cannabis significantly increases daily caloric intake and body weight in

HIV-positive patients, is well tolerated, and does not impair subjects’ cognitive

performance, according to a clinical trial published this year in the Journal of Acquired

Immune Deficiency Syndromes. Additionally, in February, investigators at San Francisco

General Hospital reported in the journal Neurology that inhaling cannabis significantly

reduced HIV-associated neuropathy (nerve pain) compared to placebo. Read the full story

at: http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7289.

See

On World AIDS Day Medical Cannabis Is Not Just A Forbidden Medicine, It is A

Forbidden Topic.

#7 Smokeless Cannabis Delivery System Found “Safe And Effective”

Vaporization is a “safe and effective” cannabinoid delivery mode for patients who desire

the rapid onset of action associated with inhalation while avoiding the respiratory risks of

smoking, according to clinical trial data published earlier this year in the journal Clinical

Pharmacology & Therapeutics. “Vaporization of marijuana does not result in exposure to

combustion gases, ... and … is an effective and apparently safe vehicle for THC delivery,”

the study concluded. Read the full story at:

http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7240.

#8 Cannabis Prohibition Costs Taxpayers More Than $40 Billion Per Year

Marijuana prohibition costs US taxpayers nearly $42 billion dollars per year in criminal

justice costs and in lost tax revenues, according to an economic analysis released in

October. Read the full story at: http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7380.

(MarijuanaNews note: The war on cannabis also has many hidden costs for

Americans and others.)

See

Lou Dobbs and the Second Mexican War. Has It Already Begun? Counting the

Costs of the Drugwar.

#9 Ninth Circuit: No “Fundamental” Right To Use Pot To Ease Suffering

The physician-approved use of cannabis to “preserve bodily integrity, avoid intolerable

pain, and preserve life” is not a Constitutionally protected right, the Ninth US Circuit

Court of Appeals ruled in March. The Court opined: “[M]edical and conventional wisdom

… recogniz[ing] the use of marijuana for medical purposes is gaining traction in the law.

But that legal recognition has not yet reached the point where a conclusion can be drawn

that the right to use medical marijuana is 'fundamental' and 'implicit in the concept of

ordered liberty.'” Read the full story at: http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7207.

(MarijuanaNews note: The Ninth Circuit is considered the most “liberal” in the

country, but they know how the Supreme Court has ruled on this issue.)

#10 FDA Advisory Panel Says Controversial Cannabinoid Blocker Not Safe For Human

Consumption

An independent FDA advisory committee determined 14-0 in June that the controversial

cannabinoid receptor antagonist Rimonabant is unsafe for human consumption in the

United States. Panelists reported that patients prescribed Rimonabant experienced

increased incidences of depression, nausea, vomiting, and suicidal tendencies. Rimonabant

is currently marketed in Europe (under the trade name Acomplia) as a dietary aid. Readthe full story at: http://www.norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=7282.
